content: Hahnemann University Hospital, established in 1885, is a medical institution located in Center City, Philadelphia. It is affiliated with Drexel University College of Medicine and serves as the Center City Hahnemann campus for the university. In 1993, Hahnemann University Hospital was acquired by Allegheny General. The following year, in 1994, the Woman's Medical College of Pennsylvania and the Medical College of Pennsylvania merged to form the MCP Hahnemann School of Medicine, which became part of the Allegheny University of the Health Sciences. However, in 1998, the parent company of Allegheny University of the Health Sciences, the Allegheny Health Education and Research Foundation, declared bankruptcy. Subsequently, Tenet Healthcare Corporation acquired the bankrupt Allegheny University, including its holdings such as Hahnemann University Hospital and other regional hospitals. These additional holdings included Roxborough Memorial Hospital, St. Christopher’s Hospital for Children, and Warminster Hospital. When Tenet acquired the holdings of Allegheny University, it established MCP Hahnemann University and arranged for Drexel University to take over its operations. In 2002, Tenet Healthcare agreed to merge MCP Hahnemann University into Drexel University for a 20-year period. Additionally, Tenet agreed to an affiliation between Drexel University College of Medicine and Tenet’s teaching hospitals in the Philadelphia area, with Hahnemann University Hospital being one of the key institutions involved in this partnership.
